## Ledger Item

Extends the catalog's commerce `Product` (`sku`, `productName`, `productType`) and adds only the accounting facts inventory posting needs:

- `assetAccount`: the inventory account a purchase of this item debits (for example `1200`, green coffee);
- `cogsAccount`: the cost-of-goods-sold account its cost moves to when it is sold or used (for example `5000`).

```ts
import { Item } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/accounting/ledger-cards';
```

Bill lines, sale lines and stock lots refer to an item by its `sku` string; a product line on a bill carries the item's asset account as its `debitAccount`.

### Operations
None.

### Bundles, prices and reorder points
`incomeAccount` and `salesPriceMinor` (per unit) are what a sale line starts from. `components` (`containsMany(BundleComponent)`: a SKU and its quantity per bundle, in thousandths) makes the product a bundle (`isBundle`): it holds no stock, and the desk's Add bundle puts one line per component on a draft invoice or sales receipt, at each component's own price, so fulfillment draws by component. `reorderPoint` and `reorderQty` (thousandths) drive the desk's Low stock list. `warehouseStock` lists the fulfilment cluster's `InventoryStock` rows for the SKU, read-only; their units are the warehouse's own, so they're shown beside the books' quantity, not reconciled with it.

### Non-goals
No price, quantity on hand or cost on the item: price lives on each sale line, cost and quantity on stock lots. The accounts are text codes, not links.

### Example
`Item/GRN-ETH-SID-2409`, an inventory lot of Ethiopia Sidamo green coffee posting to `1200` and `5000`.
